content:
maya: quick follow-up to the canary RFC — proposing an "incremental shadow + soft-fallback" pattern for AB/canary rollouts. thinking two-phase: small shadow to warm caches & validate quality, then progressive warmup with soft-fallback rules if latency/errors spike.

raj: sounds reasonable. what's the minimum shadow traffic you want to start with?

maya: start tiny — 0.5% to 2% for pure shadow (no user impact), collect correctness + perf signals. if signals look good, move to warm_pct 5-10% to exercise KV caches and batching. numbers depend on tail latency and request distribution.

sasha: main concern: cache pollution and mixed KV keys between stable and canary. recommend isolating caches per-variant and tagging shadow requests. e.g. set header `X-Shadow: true` and use `cache_namespace=variant:<id>` so shadow warms separate space.

jamie: +1. also add synthetic probe priming for common sequence lengths so we don't rely solely on live traffic. a small probe runner can emulate 95th pct seq lengths.

maya: example policy snippet for discussion:
```yaml
canary:
  shadow_pct: 1            # initial mirror fraction
  warm_pct: 5             # progressive warmup fraction
  fallbacks:
    latency_p95_ms: 1200  # threshold to trigger soft-fallback
    error_rate: 0.02      # API/model error threshold
  cache_policy: variant_namespace
  affinity: session_key    # session affinity for stateful users
```

infra-bot: deploy-bot: scheduled shadow rollout for canary/2026-05-21T09:00Z (dry-run). :gear:

raj: operational question — warm_pct increases token usage/cost. can we gate warm_pct with a budget window or autoscale credits?

jamie: we should track these metrics per-tenant and per-variant: p95 latency, error_rate, quality_delta (evals), kv_hit_rate, cold_start_count, token_cost. if warm_pct pushes cost over budget, auto-reduce warm_pct.

sasha: edge-case: frequent fallback triggers can create a feedback loop where the canary never gets enough warm time. propose hysteresis + cooldown: require threshold to be breached for N consecutive minutes, then apply cooldown_seconds after a fallback before reattempt.

maya: agreed. simple policy addition:
```yaml
fallback_policy:
  breach_window_seconds: 120
  consecutive_breaches: 3
  cooldown_seconds: 300
  min_warm_duration_seconds: 600
```

ops-runbook: add an escape hatch in the runbook: manual panic toggle that sets route=stable (100%) and posts an incident stub. include steps to pin sessions if needed.

raj: also need clear API contract for soft-fallback behavior — what downstream sees when fallback is active? return stable model id and a header `X-Fallback-Reason` so client SDKs can metric it.

maya: good call. add telemetry: emit `canary_phase` (shadow/warm/active/fallback) on each request and sample payloads (masked) for offline quality evals. tie regression alerts to a small set of prompt-based checks.

jamie: one more thought — for stateful multi-turn chat, affinity windows should be conservative (pin for 24-72h) and be overridable per-tenant. document default behaviors.

maya: thanks all. action items: 1) @sasha to prototype variant-scoped cache names and header tagging, 2) @jamie to draft probe runner and metrics dashboard, 3) @raj to propose budget gating logic, 4) infra-bot to run a dry schedule and report results. I'll iterate the RFC with these additions.

infra-bot: task created: CANARY-PRIME-312 (shadow cache isolation prototype).

ops-runbook: noted — updating runbook with panic toggle and telemetry checklist.

maya: cool — let's sync next week after prototypes. :eyes:
